Figure 1 diagram

```{r}

# Simulate data for the three reaction norm scenarios
set.seed(123)

n_lines <- 3
n_environments <- 5
environment <- seq(1, n_environments)

# Scenario 1: Genotype
genotype_only <- data.frame(
  Environment = rep(environment, n_lines),
  Genotype = rep(1:n_lines, each = n_environments),
  Phenotype = rep(seq(0, 2, length.out = n_lines), each = n_environments),
  Scenario = "Genotype"
)

# Scenario 2: Genotype + Environment
genotype_environment <- data.frame(
  Environment = rep(environment, n_lines),
  Genotype = rep(1:n_lines, each = n_environments),
  Phenotype = rep(seq(0, 2, length.out = n_lines), each = n_environments) + 
              rep(environment, n_lines),
  Scenario = "Genotype + environment"
)

# Scenario 3: Genotype x Environment
genotype_gxe <- data.frame(
  Environment = rep(environment, n_lines),
  Genotype = rep(1:n_lines, each = n_environments),
  Phenotype = rep(seq(0, 2, length.out = n_lines), each = n_environments) + 
              c(rep(1, n_environments), rep(0, n_environments), rep(-1, n_environments)) * environment,
  Scenario = "Genotype x environment"
)

# Combine all scenarios
reaction_norm_data <- rbind(genotype_only, genotype_environment, genotype_gxe)
reaction_norm_data$Scenario <- factor(reaction_norm_data$Scenario, 
                                      levels = c("Genotype", "Genotype + environment", "Genotype x environment"))

# Plot reaction norms
reaction_norm_plot <- ggplot(reaction_norm_data, aes(x = Environment, y = Phenotype, 
                                                     group = Genotype)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.5, color = "gray70") +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Environment", y = "Phenotype", color = "Genotype") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

# Simulate data for evolutionary change
n <- 1000

# Plasticity-first evolution: High rate of phenotypic change
plasticity_first <- data.frame(
  Plasticity = rnorm(n, mean = 2, sd = 0.5),
  Phenotype = pmax(rnorm(n, mean = 4, sd = 0.5), 0),
  Selection = rnorm(n, mean = 0.2, sd = 0.05),
  Scenario = "Plasticity-first"
)

# Canalization: High rate of phenotypic change
canalization <- data.frame(
  Plasticity = rnorm(n, mean = -2, sd = 0.5),
  Phenotype = pmax(rnorm(n, mean = 4, sd = 0.5), 0),
  Selection = rnorm(n, mean = -0.2, sd = 0.05),
  Scenario = "Canalization"
)

# Plasticity-buffered evolution: Low rate of phenotypic change near 0
plasticity_buffered <- data.frame(
  Plasticity = rnorm(n, mean = 1, sd = 0.5),
  Phenotype = pmax(rnorm(n, mean = 0.5, sd = 0.1), 0),
  Selection = rnorm(n, mean = 0.2, sd = 0.05),
  Scenario = "Plasticity-buffered"
)

# Combine data
evolution_data <- rbind(plasticity_first, canalization, plasticity_buffered)

# Plot histograms for plasticity and selection coefficients
plasticity_histogram <- ggplot(evolution_data, aes(x = Plasticity)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 1, fill = "gray", position = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Rates of Evolutionary Change: Plasticity", x = "Plasticity", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

phenotype_histogram <- ggplot(evolution_data, aes(x = Phenotype)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 1, fill = "gray", position = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Rate of phenotypic evolution", x = "Evolutionary rate", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

selection_histogram <- ggplot(evolution_data, aes(x = Selection)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 1, fill = "gray", position = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Selection on plasticity", x = "Selection coefficient", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

# Combine evolutionary plots
evolution_plots <- ggarrange(phenotype_histogram, selection_histogram, 
                             labels = c("", ""), ncol = 1, nrow = 2)

# --- Combine All Plots ---
Fig1_rev <- ggarrange(reaction_norm_plot, evolution_plots, 
                      labels = c("A", "B"),
                      heights = c(.5, 1),
                      ncol = 1, nrow = 2)

# Display final plot
print(Fig1_rev)

# Export the comparison plot as PNG
png("~/Documents/GitHub/PFE_perspective/Fig1_rev.png", 
    units = "in", width = 12, height = 12, res = 600)
Fig1_rev
dev.off()
```

Figure 2 simulation of epistatic PFE

```{r}

# Parameters
set.seed(42)
generations <- 100
population_size <- 1000
recomb_rate <- 0.02
drift_sd <- 0.005
temperature <- seq(20, 35, length.out = generations) + rnorm(generations, sd = 0.5)

# Initial haplotype frequencies
freqs <- data.frame(
  generation = 1:generations,
  axbx = 0.0,   # Completely purged initially
  axby = 0.10,  # Initial frequency
  other = 0.90  # Other haplotypes
)

# Selection coefficients for scenarios
selection_scenario1 <- function(temp) {
  list(
    axbx = ifelse(temp > 30, 0.15, ifelse(temp > 25, -0.05, -0.15)),
    axby = ifelse(temp > 18 & temp < 28, 0.05, ifelse(temp > 28, -0.05, 0))
  )
}
selection_scenario2 <- function(temp) {
  list(
    axbx = ifelse(temp > 30, 0.15, ifelse(temp > 25, -0.05, -0.15)),
    axby = 0  # Neutral under all conditions
  )
}

# Simulation function
simulate_haplotypes <- function(selection_function) {
  results <- freqs
  recombination_events <- numeric(generations)
  
  for (t in 2:generations) {
    temp <- temperature[t]
    sel <- selection_function(temp)
    
    # Recombination: Stronger dependence on axby and bx alleles
    recombination_events[t] <- recomb_rate * results$axby[t-1] * results$other[t-1]
    new_axbx <- recombination_events[t]
    
    # Selection and drift
    axbx_fit <- results$axbx[t-1] + sel$axbx * results$axbx[t-1] + new_axbx
    axby_fit <- results$axby[t-1] + sel$axby * results$axby[t-1] - new_axbx
    
    # Drift
    axbx_fit <- axbx_fit + rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = drift_sd)
    axby_fit <- axby_fit + rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = drift_sd)
    
    # Normalize frequencies
    other_fit <- max(0, 1 - axbx_fit - axby_fit)
    total <- axbx_fit + axby_fit + other_fit
    
    results$axbx[t] <- max(0, axbx_fit / total)
    results$axby[t] <- max(0, axby_fit / total)
    results$other[t] <- max(0, other_fit / total)
  }
  
  results$recombination <- recombination_events
  results
}

# Run simulations for both scenarios
scenario1 <- simulate_haplotypes(selection_scenario1)
scenario1$scenario <- "PFE"

scenario2 <- simulate_haplotypes(selection_scenario2)
scenario2$scenario <- "Neutral plasticity"

# Update for relabeling and adding selection coefficients over time
scenario1 <- scenario1 %>%
  mutate(sel_axbx = map_dbl(1:generations, ~ selection_scenario1(temperature[.x])$axbx),
         sel_axby = map_dbl(1:generations, ~ selection_scenario1(temperature[.x])$axby))

scenario2 <- scenario2 %>%
  mutate(sel_axbx = map_dbl(1:generations, ~ selection_scenario2(temperature[.x])$axbx),
         sel_axby = map_dbl(1:generations, ~ selection_scenario2(temperature[.x])$axby))

# Combine results
results <- bind_rows(scenario1, scenario2) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(axbx, axby, other), names_to = "haplotype", values_to = "frequency")

# Separate datasets for clarity
selection_results <- results %>%
  filter(haplotype == "axbx") %>%
  select(generation, scenario, sel_axbx, sel_axby) %>%
  distinct()

recombination_results <- results %>%
  filter(haplotype == "axbx") %>%
  select(generation, scenario, recombination) %>%
  distinct()

temperature_results <- data.frame(
  generation = 1:generations,
  temperature = temperature,
  scenario = rep(c("PFE", "Neutral plasticity"), each = generations)
)

# Plotting
library(patchwork)

# Temperature over time
plot_temp <- ggplot(temperature_results, aes(x = generation, y = temperature)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = "Environment", x = "Generation") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Recombination events leading to axbx
plot_recomb <- ggplot(recombination_results, aes(x = generation, y = recombination)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "axbx formed by recombination", y = "Recombination events", x = "Generation") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Frequencies of haplotypes
plot_haplotypes <- ggplot(results, aes(x = generation, y = frequency, color = haplotype)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = "Frequency", x = "Generation", , color = "Haplotype") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("axbx" = "red", "axby" = "orange", "other" = "gray")) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# Selection coefficients
plot_selection <- ggplot(selection_results, aes(x = generation)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = sel_axbx, color = "axbx"), size = 1, se = FALSE, span = .1) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = sel_axby, color = "axby"), size = 1, se = FALSE, span = .1) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  labs( y = "Selection coefficient", x = "Generation", color = "Haplotype") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("axbx" = "red", "axby" = "orange")) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

library(ggpubr)

# Combine plots into a grid with ggarrange
final_plot <- ggarrange(
  plot_temp, 
  plot_recomb, 
  plot_selection, 
  plot_haplotypes, 
  ncol = 2, nrow = 2, 
  labels = c("A", "B", "C", "D")
)

# Display the combined plot
# Export the comparison plot as PNG
png("~/Documents/GitHub/PFE_perspective/Fig_2rev.png", 
    units = "in", width = 12, height = 12, res = 600)
final_plot
dev.off()

```

Simulation without assumptions about mutation rate, recombination rate, or population size

```{r}

setwd("~/Documents/GitHub/PFE_perspective/arg_sim/")

# Load necessary library
library(Biostrings)

# Define parameters
total_length <- 100000  # 100 kb region
num_individuals <- 10   # Population size
num_generations <- 50   # Number of generations
alleles <- c("A", "T", "C", "G")  # Possible nucleotides
gene_length <- total_length / 2   # Length for each haplotype
mutation_rate <- 0.001  # Mutation rate per site

# Function to initialize the population with random haplotypes
initialize_population <- function(n, gene_length) {
  population <- data.frame(
    Hap_A1 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")),
    Hap_A2 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")),
    Hap_B1 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")),
    Hap_B2 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = ""))
  )
  return(population)
}

# Function to introduce mutations
mutate_haplotype <- function(haplotype, mutation_rate) {
  seq_split <- unlist(strsplit(haplotype, ""))
  mutate_indices <- which(runif(length(seq_split)) < mutation_rate)
  seq_split[mutate_indices] <- sample(alleles, length(mutate_indices), replace = TRUE)
  return(paste(seq_split, collapse = ""))
}

mutate_population <- function(population, mutation_rate) {
  population[] <- lapply(population, function(hap) sapply(hap, mutate_haplotype, mutation_rate))
  return(population)
}

# Function to perform recombination
recombine <- function(population) {
  n <- nrow(population)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    partner <- sample(seq_len(n), 1)
    if (runif(1) < 0.5) {
      temp <- population$Hap_A2[i]
      population$Hap_A2[i] <- population$Hap_A2[partner]
      population$Hap_A2[partner] <- temp
    }
    if (runif(1) < 0.5) {
      temp <- population$Hap_B2[i]
      population$Hap_B2[i] <- population$Hap_B2[partner]
      population$Hap_B2[partner] <- temp
    }
  }
  return(population)
}

# Function to apply selection while maintaining population size
apply_selection <- function(population, selection_criteria) {
  selected <- switch(
    selection_criteria,
    "plastic" = which(substr(population$Hap_A1, 1, 1) == "A" & substr(population$Hap_B1, 1, 1) == "C"),
    "canalized" = which(substr(population$Hap_A1, 1, 1) == "T" & substr(population$Hap_B1, 1, 1) == "G")
  )
  
  # Ensure selected population is exactly num_individuals
  if (length(selected) < num_individuals) {
    additional <- sample(seq_len(nrow(population)), num_individuals - length(selected), replace = TRUE)
    selected <- c(selected, additional)
  } else if (length(selected) > num_individuals) {
    selected <- sample(selected, num_individuals)
  }
  
  return(population[selected, , drop = FALSE])
}

# Function to generate high-depth sequences by replicating haplotypes
generate_high_depth_sequences <- function(population, depth_per_individual = 20) {
  high_depth_sequences <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(population))) {
    # Replicate each individual’s haplotype pair (A1 + B1, A2 + B2) multiple times to simulate read depth
    for (j in 1:depth_per_individual) {
      high_depth_sequences <- c(high_depth_sequences, paste(population$Hap_A1[i], population$Hap_B1[i], sep = ""))
      high_depth_sequences <- c(high_depth_sequences, paste(population$Hap_A2[i], population$Hap_B2[i], sep = ""))
    }
  }
  
  return(high_depth_sequences)
}

# Generate DNA sequences for output
generate_dna_sequences <- function(population) {
  sequences <- c(
    paste(population$Hap_A1, population$Hap_B1, sep = ""),
    paste(population$Hap_A2, population$Hap_B2, sep = "")
  )
  return(sequences)
}

# Initialize population
population <- initialize_population(num_individuals, gene_length)

# Simulate over generations
for (generation in seq_len(num_generations)) {
  # Reproduction: Create offspring by sampling parents
  offspring <- population[sample(seq_len(nrow(population)), num_individuals, replace = TRUE), ]
  
  # Mutation
  offspring <- mutate_population(offspring, mutation_rate)
  
  # Recombination
  offspring <- recombine(offspring)
  
  # Selection
  offspring <- apply_selection(offspring, "plastic")
  
  # Update population
  population <- offspring
}

# Generate final high-depth DNA sequences by replicating each individual’s haplotypes
final_high_depth_sequences <- generate_high_depth_sequences(population, depth_per_individual = 50)  # Set desired read depth per individual

# Create sequence names
seq_names <- paste0("Individual_", rep(seq_len(num_individuals), each = 2 * 50), "_Hap_", rep(c("1", "2"), each = 50), "_Rep_", rep(1:50, times = num_individuals))

# Convert character vector to DNAStringSet
fasta_sequences <- DNAStringSet(sapply(final_high_depth_sequences, DNAString))

# Assign names to the sequences
names(fasta_sequences) <- seq_names

# Output separate FASTA files for each individual
for (i in 1:num_individuals) {
  # Correctly subset 100 sequences per individual (50 reads for each haplotype)
  individual_sequences <- fasta_sequences[((i - 1) * 100 + 1):(i * 100)]  
  writeXStringSet(individual_sequences, paste0("Individual_", i, "_high_depth.fasta"))
}

# Reference sequence
reference_sequence <- individual_sequences[[1]]

# Convert to a DNAStringSet object
reference_fasta <- DNAStringSet(DNAString(reference_sequence))

# Assign a name to the reference sequence
names(reference_fasta) <- "Individual_1_Hap_1"

# Write the reference genome to a FASTA file
writeXStringSet(reference_fasta, "reference_genome.fasta")

# ----------------------------------------------
# Align each individual’s reads to the reference genome
for (i in 1:num_individuals) {
  # Align the reads of each individual to the reference
  system(paste("bwa index reference_genome.fasta"))  # Index the reference genome
  system(paste("bwa mem reference_genome.fasta Individual_", i, "_high_depth.fasta > Individual_", i, "_aligned_reads.sam", sep = ""))  # Perform the alignment

  # Convert SAM to BAM
  system(paste("samtools view -Sb Individual_", i, "_aligned_reads.sam > Individual_", i, "_aligned_reads.bam", sep = ""))
  
  # Sort and index the BAM file
  system(paste("samtools sort Individual_", i, "_aligned_reads.bam -o Individual_", i, "_aligned_reads_sorted.bam", sep = ""))
  system(paste("samtools index Individual_", i, "_aligned_reads_sorted.bam", sep = ""))
  
  # Call variants from the BAM file
  system(paste("bcftools mpileup -O v -f reference_genome.fasta Individual_", i, "_aligned_reads_sorted.bam | bcftools call -mv -Ov -o Individual_", i, "_raw_variants.vcf", sep = ""))
  
  # **Filter for biallelic SNPs only**
  system(paste("bcftools view -v snps -m2 -M2 Individual_", i, "_raw_variants.vcf > Individual_", i, "_biallelic_variants.vcf", sep = ""))
}

# Print out the first few lines of the VCF files to verify
system("cat Individual_1_variants.vcf")

```

Merge simulated vcf's

```{bash}

# Compress and index each VCF file
for vcf in *.vcf; do
  bgzip -c "$vcf" > "${vcf}.gz"
  tabix -p vcf "${vcf}.gz"
done

# Merge individual VCF files into a single VCF
bcftools merge -Ov -o merged_variants.vcf *biallelic_variants.vcf.gz

```

Second approach

```{r}

# Load necessary library
library(Biostrings)

# Define parameters
total_length <- 100000  # 100 kb region
num_individuals <- 10   # Population size
num_generations <- 50   # Number of generations
alleles <- c("A", "T", "C", "G")  # Possible nucleotides
gene_length <- total_length / 2   # Length for each haplotype
mutation_rate <- 0.001  # Mutation rate per site

# Function to initialize the population with random haplotypes
initialize_population <- function(n, gene_length) {
  population <- data.frame(
    Hap_A1 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")),
    Hap_A2 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")),
    Hap_B1 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")),
    Hap_B2 = replicate(n, paste(sample(alleles, gene_length, replace = TRUE), collapse = ""))
  )
  return(population)
}

# Function to introduce mutations
mutate_haplotype <- function(haplotype, mutation_rate) {
  seq_split <- unlist(strsplit(haplotype, ""))
  mutate_indices <- which(runif(length(seq_split)) < mutation_rate)
  seq_split[mutate_indices] <- sample(alleles, length(mutate_indices), replace = TRUE)
  return(paste(seq_split, collapse = ""))
}

mutate_population <- function(population, mutation_rate) {
  population[] <- lapply(population, function(hap) sapply(hap, mutate_haplotype, mutation_rate))
  return(population)
}

# Function to perform recombination
recombine <- function(population) {
  n <- nrow(population)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    partner <- sample(seq_len(n), 1)
    if (runif(1) < 0.5) {
      temp <- population$Hap_A2[i]
      population$Hap_A2[i] <- population$Hap_A2[partner]
      population$Hap_A2[partner] <- temp
    }
    if (runif(1) < 0.5) {
      temp <- population$Hap_B2[i]
      population$Hap_B2[i] <- population$Hap_B2[partner]
      population$Hap_B2[partner] <- temp
    }
  }
  return(population)
}

# Function to apply selection while maintaining population size
apply_selection <- function(population, selection_criteria) {
  selected <- switch(
    selection_criteria,
    "plastic" = which(substr(population$Hap_A1, 1, 1) == "A" & substr(population$Hap_B1, 1, 1) == "C"),
    "canalized" = which(substr(population$Hap_A1, 1, 1) == "T" & substr(population$Hap_B1, 1, 1) == "G")
  )
  
  # Ensure selected population is exactly num_individuals
  if (length(selected) < num_individuals) {
    additional <- sample(seq_len(nrow(population)), num_individuals - length(selected), replace = TRUE)
    selected <- c(selected, additional)
  } else if (length(selected) > num_individuals) {
    selected <- sample(selected, num_individuals)
  }
  
  return(population[selected, , drop = FALSE])
}

# Generate DNA sequences for output
generate_dna_sequences <- function(population) {
  sequences <- c(
    paste(population$Hap_A1, population$Hap_B1, sep = ""),
    paste(population$Hap_A2, population$Hap_B2, sep = "")
  )
  return(sequences)
}

# Initialize population
population <- initialize_population(num_individuals, gene_length)

# Simulate over generations
for (generation in seq_len(num_generations)) {
  # Reproduction: Create offspring by sampling parents
  offspring <- population[sample(seq_len(nrow(population)), num_individuals, replace = TRUE), ]
  
  # Mutation
  offspring <- mutate_population(offspring, mutation_rate)
  
  # Recombination
  offspring <- recombine(offspring)
  
  # Selection
  offspring <- apply_selection(offspring, "plastic")
  
  # Update population
  population <- offspring
}

# Generate final DNA sequences
final_sequences <- generate_dna_sequences(population)

# Create sequence names
seq_names <- paste0("Individual_", rep(seq_len(num_individuals), each = 2), "_Hap_", c("1", "2"))

# Convert sequences into a Biostrings object and write to FASTA
fasta_sequences <- DNAStringSet(final_sequences)
names(fasta_sequences) <- seq_names
writeXStringSet(fasta_sequences, "simulated_population.fasta")

# Print the first few sequences to verify
head(fasta_sequences)

# Select a haplotype to be used as the reference genome (e.g., Individual_1_Hap_1)
reference_sequence <- final_sequences[1]  # Assuming the first sequence is Individual_1_Hap_1
reference_fasta <- DNAStringSet(reference_sequence)

# Assign a name to the reference sequence
names(reference_fasta) <- "Individual_1_Hap_1"

# Write the reference genome to a FASTA file
writeXStringSet(reference_fasta, "reference_genome.fasta")

# ----------------------------------------------
# Align the simulated sequences to the reference genome

# Assuming you have BWA or another aligner installed on the system
# This step would be done via system calls or external software (BWA, Minimap2, etc.)
# The alignment process would generate a BAM file

system("bwa index reference_genome.fasta")  # Index the reference genome
system("bwa mem reference_genome.fasta simulated_population.fasta > aligned_reads.sam")  # Perform the alignment

# Convert SAM to BAM
system("samtools view -Sb aligned_reads.sam > aligned_reads.bam")

# Sort and index the BAM file
system("samtools sort aligned_reads.bam -o aligned_reads_sorted.bam")
system("samtools index aligned_reads_sorted.bam")

# ----------------------------------------------
# Call variants from the BAM file

# Create a VCF file using the `bcftools` command line tool
system("bcftools mpileup -O v -f reference_genome.fasta aligned_reads_sorted.bam | bcftools call -mv -Ov -o variants.vcf")

# Print out the first few lines of the VCF file to verify
system("head variants.vcf")

```

argweaver code

```{bash}

# Load dependencies
```

Wrangling argweaver samples

```{python}

def extract_newick_trees(file_path, output_path):
    """
    Extracts Newick format trees from a file and saves them to a new file.

    Parameters:
        file_path (str): Path to the input file containing Newick trees.
        output_path (str): Path to save the extracted Newick trees.
    """
    trees = []

    with open(file_path, 'r') as file:
        for line in file:
            if line.startswith('TREE'):
                # Extract the Newick tree part from the line
                parts = line.strip().split('\t')
                if len(parts) > 3:
                    newick_tree = parts[3]
                    trees.append(newick_tree)

    # Save extracted trees to output file
    with open(output_path, 'w') as output_file:
        for tree in trees:
            output_file.write(tree + '\n\n')

# Example usage
input_file = '/hb/home/snbogan/pfe/argweaver_sim1.100.smc'  # Replace with your input file path
output_file = 'newick_trees.txt'  # Replace with your desired output file path
extract_newick_trees(input_file, output_file)

```

Extract specific newick trees from sampled geneologies and create mock allele frequencies for first test

```{bash}

sed -n "5p" newick_trees.txt > gen5.newick

for i in {1..20}; do echo "$RANDOM / 32768" | bc -l; done > freq.txt

```
